rule: A signed bundle is a PAL-CBOR map { body, sigEd25519, sigMldsa65 }. msg = ascii(domain) || SHA-384(body). Bundle: domain "pal3-ext-bundle-v1", ML-DSA context "pal3-ext-sig-v1", signed by signerEdPk and signerDsaPk of the body. Publisher certificate: domain "pal3-ext-publisher-cert-v1", ML-DSA context "pal3-ext-cert-v1", signed by the issuing trusted root. Both signatures MUST verify. The signer is accepted when it equals a trusted root, or when body.publisherCert is a certificate issued by a trusted root whose subject keys equal the signer. All signatures are made in the deterministic ML-DSA mode.

bundles.name: rootSignedBundle
bundles.description: A bundle signed directly by a trusted root

bundles.name: publisherDelegatedBundle
bundles.description: A bundle signed by a publisher whose certificate (publisherCert in the body) was issued by the trusted root and covers com.vector.*

bundles.name: bundleWithEmptyOperations
bundles.description: A root-signed bundle that declares no operation and no TLV tag

publisherCertificates.name: publisherCertificate
publisherCertificates.description: The certificate of vector-publisher: the issuer is the trusted root, the subject is the publisher keys of publisherDelegatedBundle

rejected.name: strippedMldsaSignature
rejected.description: The ML-DSA-65 signature of a root-signed bundle is removed: strict-AND fails

rejected.name: flippedEd25519Signature
rejected.description: One bit of the Ed25519 signature is flipped

rejected.name: tamperedBody
rejected.description: The bundle name is changed after signing

rejected.name: selfSignedBundle
rejected.description: A valid signature by a key that is neither a trusted root nor backed by a publisher certificate

rejected.name: certificateOfAnotherKey
rejected.description: The bundle signer presents the publisher certificate of another key

rejected.name: bundleSignedUnderTheCertificateLabel
rejected.description: A bundle body signed with the publisher-certificate message prefix instead of the bundle prefix
